Sorry again for the delay in this review, it's been busy and the validation logic is complex.

I think that using create tests for validating updates as you've done here is a bad idea. It's a totally different organization from what the code is doing now, and will leave us in a state with a lot of create validations also being called from updates and the control flow generally being tangled. 

In other words, we shouldn't be adding oldX to any of the ValidateX() methods, and should use/create ValidateXUpdate() methods instead.

If we want to unify the create and update code the way you have partially done here, we should be really intentional about it, and not make a PR like this that leaves things in an in-between state. All this validation code is hard enough to understand is at is.

The way I see this change, we need to update validation of PersistentVolumeClaimsSpec, which is used in PersistentVolumeClaim and PersistentVolumeClaimTemplate>EphemeralVolumeSource>VolumeSource>Volume which appears in pods and so things that use a pod template. Some of these can't be updated (statefulsets), so no additional validation is needed; others can (daemonsets).

I think it would be more in keeping with existing code to update ValidatePersistentVolumeClaimUpdate, ValidatePodUpdate, ValidatePodTemplateUpdate, plumb down the various Validate*Update methods the appropriate ValidatePersistentVolumeClaimUpdate, ValidatePodTemplateUpdate, etc.

lmk if you have questions.

Look through other update functions for examples on how to reduce duplication by reusing ValidateX(), eg https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/apis/apps/validation/validation.go#L176 where a copy of the updated resource is made, the (few) fields that can be updated are copied from the old one, equality is checked to confirm only the allowed updates are made. issue_context.title: PVC resource limits not validated
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

PVC never supported setting capacity limits. However, it looks like in validation, we never enforced it: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a5622f3f6e1f5d5ffd066d799204ea0c6d1a49e2/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L2124

This means that it's possible PVC.spce.resource.limits could have garbage values in them. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Validation should have rejected PVC setting resource.limits. 

If we want to tighten validation, we would need to think about how to do it carefully for existing objects. Also, we should consider if we want to support limits.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a PVC and set resource.limits

### Anything else we need to know?

@msau42  Here is the fix proposal, your comment would be appreciated.
1. The tighten validation would be added, which means, if `spec.Resources.Limits[core.ResourceStorage]` is present, no matter what value in them, the validation will failed with error indication.
2. Regarding pvc supports limit or not , IMHO, No. Since the storage claimed by pvc can not be shared with another pvc, the pvc limit may not work as the request&limits of CPU or Memory.

This would be a small size PR, @NikhilSharmaWe maybe you can help to review the above idea and the following PR later. Thanks

I don't think we can just add validation, because there may be resources out there that have set the limit, and we don't want to break those clusters.

If we know that we want to start using limits, eg plumb them through to the csi driver, then we want to start validating the the limit is a valid storage quantity. If we don't have a plan for using limits, then it's not as clear to me what to do---perhaps start warning, in order to make it easier to add some features in the future.

The other dimension to think about is how to validate. Adding API validation is problematic, as mentioned, because it could break existing clusters. I think that means the option is to add a webhook that will warn on invalid PVC, and then we can ratchet that to enforcement over several k8s versions, and only then move this into api validation.

Or are there other options here?
(fyi, it looks like key people are out during the holiday time, so responses might be delayed)

review_comments: Is this correct to remove this check? Don't we need to do a deep copy + clean, otherwise we miss validating some other part of the JobSped?

I think it is correct to remove the check :-)
As `ValidateUpdate` --> `ValidateJobUpdate` --> `ValidateJobSpecUpdate`, and in  `ValidateUpdate` we already do the deep copy + clean, and invoke `ValidateJob` to do the validating on the JobSpec. Thus it's better to remove the redundant check.

Ok. It looks like other Validate*Update functions don't always call the non-update validation so you aren't introducing a new inconsistency here. I worry a little that future changes may miss the fact that it's assumed the JobSpec is validated somewhere by the caller, but as I said that seems to be the standard.
add tests for the cases mentioned above where the volumes are added/deleted.
added a new function`TestValidateVolumesUpdate` for the test cases mentioned

If there is an update that creates a volume in the spec, will that get checked for not having limits? I don't see where that's done.

See comment below in the tests.
Yeah, the check is not here, but in the previous `validatePodMetadataAndSpec` , `ValidateDaemonSetSpec`, `ValidateDeploymentSpec`, `ValidateXXXSpec`, etc
I feel like we're making it harder to reason about where these checks will take place, but maybe the api approver can comment on this style of doing things.

This doesn't strike me as the right way to do it. It seems the idea is that if there is a different number of new volumes, we're assuming they are all new, and let the ValidateVolumes handle it, but if the number is the same, it's an update?

But that may not be true, eg a volume may be deleted and another updated, or a volume may be deleted and another added. Worse, the order of the volumes could be rearranged, in which case the update check is incorrect.

I think old and new should be correlated by Volume.Name and then an update check done on matching names to confirm the limits aren't set only in that case.

IIUC for other volumes, the limit check is verified in the non-update validation (?---can you confirm? Maybe that doesn't work correctly for existing volumes that have the limits set (which we want to allow)).

Yeah, check the number of new volumes against the old one is not correct. I have modified it to correlate Volume.Name of old and new volumes and do the udpate check accordingly.

You are right, for other volumes it doesn't work correctly for existing volumes that have the limits set. I have fixed ths problem.

Add a comment describing what this function does & how it's used.

(and in other places where you've added a function)
